research_rationale: EO 11667 (April 19, 1972; 37 FR 7763) was read in the held official Federal Register scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF pages 7-8: heading, preamble, sections 1-3, signature block and FR Doc. 72-6171 filing line, so the text is complete). Its operative content is the establishment and composition of the President's Advisory Committee on the Environmental Merit Awards Program (sec. 1(a)), three committee functions (sec. 1(b)), the no-compensation/travel-expense rule (sec. 2) and EPA administrative support (sec. 3); the preamble is narrative. The order has no expiry, sunset, report deadline or condition. Because the committee existed before the Federal Advisory Committee Act took effect (January 5, 1973), it would have terminated on January 5, 1975 unless renewed; EO 11827 section 1(8) (held, 40 FR 1218) renewed it until January 5, 1977. Before that date EO 11948 (held, 41 FR 55706) section 4(a)(1) revoked EO 11667, and section 5 makes EO 11948 effective December 31, 1976; section 3's separate January 16, 1977 date applies only to EO 11868. So the first and only end of every clause is the revocation effective December 31, 1976, and the whole-order end is that date. The OFR catalog (revoked by EO 11948; continued by EO 11827) and the 1989 OFR Codification disposition table (continued by EO 11827; revoked by EO 11948) agree, and no other amendment, revocation or statute affecting the order was found in the bounded searches listed (no U.S. Code or eCFR citation of the order). Quotations are the scan's OCR text, kept as printed (soft hyphens at line ends).

research_rationale: EO 11864 (June 13, 1975; 40 FR 25579) was read in the held official FR scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF page 11, complete from heading to FR Doc. 75-15839 and footnote). It is a single amending sentence: effective June 1, 1975, section 1 of EO 11861 (placing positions in level IV of the Executive Schedule) is revised at paragraph (13) to read 'Adviser to the Secretary (Counselor, Economic Policy Board), Department of the Treasury, to terminate effective August 1, 1975' (the OCR renders the closing '1975.”' with its footnote mark as '1,197571'; EO 11877 section 1(b), held, quotes the same paragraph with the date as 'August 1, 1975'). The order therefore fixed its own end: the placement lapsed on August 1, 1975, and that is the first end of the only clause and the whole-order end. The formal supersession came a month later: EO 11877 (September 2, 1975; 40 FR 40797, held), which states no effective date, superseded EO 11864 (section 2) and replaced paragraph (13) with an open-ended placement (section 1(b)); it is recorded as a later event, not as the first end, following the rule that a formal supersession can follow an earlier cessation under the order's own terms. A current-law note at 5 U.S.C. 5317 and the OFR catalog describe the same history (the note says the paragraph was 'to terminate effective August 1, 1975' and was superseded by EO 11877); the 1989 OFR Codification table lists EO 11864 as amending EO 11861 and superseded by EO 11877. The machine current-law hits for this order are that historical note, not a continuing basis.

research_rationale: EO 10529 (April 22, 1954; 19 FR 2397) was read in the held official FR scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF pages 1-3: heading, enacting clause, sections 1-5, Eisenhower signature and FR Doc. 54-3141). Section 2 begins on page 2397 and continues on page 2399 after the issue's contents pages; the clause is quoted from page 2399. Operative clauses: the Administrator's recommendation of volunteer Federal personnel for State and local pre-emergency civil-defense training (sec. 1); the agency head's year-to-year authorization (sec. 2) and its three conditions (sec. 2(a)-(c)); continued pay, status and travel (sec. 3); a construction rule (sec. 4); and two definitions (sec. 5). There is no expiry, condition or report duty. Later events, read in the held texts: EO 10773 (July 1, 1958), EO 10782 (effective August 26, 1958, renaming the office in EO 10773's substituted references) and EO 11051 section 603(d) (September 27, 1962) only substituted the responsible officials (ODCM/OCDM Director, then OEP Director or Secretary of Defense); they are amendments, not ends. Section 1's reference to section 3 of EO 10346 describes the arrangements the recommendations serve; EO 10346 was revoked by EO 11490 in 1969, but section 1 does not make its own authority depend on EO 10346, and EO 10529 was still being maintained by amendment, so that revocation is not treated as an end. EO 12148 (signed July 20, 1979; 44 FR 43239, held) section 5-104 revokes EO 10529, as amended, and section 6 makes the order effective July 15, 1979; that stated effective date is the first end of every clause and the whole-order end. The OFR catalog and the 1989 OFR Codification disposition table (amended by EOs 10773, 11051; revoked by EO 12148) agree. The current-law machine hits for this order are U.S. Code editorial notes recording its amendments and its revocation by EO 12148, not a continuing basis. No other amendment, revocation or statute affecting EO 10529 was found in the bounded searches listed.

research_rationale: EO 12489 (September 28, 1984; 49 FR 38927) was read in the held official FR scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF pages 9-10, complete from heading to FR Doc. 84-26328). Ends: section 2 expired by its own terms on December 31, 1984; no later continuance of the Task Force exists in the saved catalog (EO 12395 is noted only as continued by EOs 12399 and 12489 and revoked by EO 12534), and EO 12534 section 3(c) revoked EO 12395 as an order whose committee had terminated. None of the eleven section 1 committees was terminated before September 30, 1985: EO 12534 section 1 (held) continues all eleven again, and the catalog shows no intervening revocation. EO 12534 (September 30, 1985; 50 FR 40319, held) section 4 supersedes EO 12489 and section 5 makes it effective September 30, 1985, which is also the last day of EO 12489's own continuance term; that date is the first end of section 1, its items and section 3, and the whole-order end. The OFR catalog (superseded by EO 12534) and the 1989 OFR Codification disposition table (superseded by EO 12534) agree; no U.S. Code or eCFR citation of EO 12489 was found.

research_rationale: EO 11809 (September 30, 1974; 39 FR 35565) was read in the held official FR scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF page 15, heading to FR Doc. 74-23127). Its five operative sections establish the President's Labor-Management Committee (eight labor, eight management members and a neutral coordinator), state its study-and-advice functions, direct it to encourage sector labor-management committees, direct agency cooperation and assign FACA functions to the Treasury. EO 11948 (held) section 4(a)(2) revokes it, effective December 31, 1976 under section 5. Because the Committee was created after January 5, 1973 and is absent from EO 11827's list of continued post-1973 committees, it may have terminated under the FACA two-year rule about three months before the formal revocation; the first ends are therefore left open rather than taken from the revocation. The OFR catalog (revoked by EO 11948; see EO 11849) and the 1989 OFR Codification table (revoked by EO 11948) agree on the formal history.
